title: serve: preserve tool prefixes for tool_choice=none
body:
## Summary

Keep tool declarations in the Chat Completions prompt when `tool_choice` is `"none"`, while independently disabling structured tool-call output and the MCP tool-execution loop.

A client can keep its conversation and tools unchanged, append a summarization/compaction instruction, and set `tool_choice: "none"`. Currently `_openai()` replaces `tools` with `None`. Because the model's template puts tool declarations near the beginning, this changes the leading prompt tokens and prevents an otherwise matching conversation checkpoint from being reused. A long context is not necessary to reproduce this input-prefix mismatch.

Related: #1222 addressed Codex/Responses compaction. This PR targets `/v1/chat/completions`; it does not change the Responses compaction mechanism or require client/session metadata.

## What changed

- Retain prompt tool declarations for `tool_choice: "none"`.
- Add keyword-only `parse_tools=True` to `OutputParser` and `Service.run`. Chat Completions sets it to false for `none`, including disabling recovery of calls inside reasoning. Preserve the existing `tool_call_recovery` option for other requests.
- Do not enter `run_with_mcp` under `none`; MCP declarations can remain in the prompt without executing model-requested tools.
- Preserve acceptance of `response_format` with tool declarations when `tool_choice` is `none`; the existing structured-output/MCP restriction remains.
- Add regression coverage for equal absent/auto/none prompt tokens, streamed/non-streamed responses, thinking on/off, split and truncated tool markup, recovery on/off, MCP non-execution, and JSON response format.

If the model writes tool-shaped text under `none`, it is returned as ordinary reasoning/content, **not** `tool_calls` or a `tool_calls` finish reason. This is an output-parsing/execution restriction, not a new grammar or sampling constraint.

Normal `auto`/absent/required/named behavior, Responses and Anthropic routing, the native engine, and KV formats/policies are left alone. The branch is based directly on upstream `fb58e0dbc8399662c0e47c76578c6e878b14f6cf` and contains only this change, in four Python files.

## Validation

### CPU/mock regressions

```sh
python -m unittest \
  serve.test_frontend serve.test_server serve.test_reasoning_tools \
  serve.test_structured serve.test_responses serve.test_mcp
```

**372 tests passed** on the PR worktree. No GPU backend files changed.

### Short-context prefix reproduction

Compared unmodified upstream `fb58e0d` with this patch using the real model tokenizer/chat template, actual isolated HTTP handlers, and `MockEngine` generation. The fixture has two tool definitions and 128 short synthetic records, followed by an assistant reply and a summarization request with `tool_choice: "none"`. The context limit is 4096 tokens.

| Measurement | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Ordinary request input tokens | 3196 | 3196 |
| Appended compaction request input tokens | 2948 | 3237 |
| Common prefix with ordinary request | 41 | 3196 |
| Native prefix predicate's matching length | 0 | 3191 |

The ordinary request's token sequence is identical before/after. For the final row, a **synthetic checkpoint token sequence** ending before the first assistant turn (3191 tokens) was supplied to the **unmodified upstream C++ `conversation_prefix`** function.

This checks HTTP rendering and native **token matching only**: no actual KV/GDN snapshot was captured or restored, and no GPU inference or cache-hit/performance benchmark was performed. It removes this specific source of prefix invalidation; it does not guarantee hits when other prompt content or checkpoint boundaries change.

body:
Issue: Resolves #676

## Summary

A chat list in the left sidebar, kept in `localStorage`, opt-in: the switch is off by default, and off is the page from the last release. This is the `serve/web/app.js` + `localStorage` work you said was welcome on #361; #676 is the open request for it.

## What changed

**`serve/web/app.js`**
- The switch (`strata.history`, off by default) and the chat list (`strata.chats`): entries of `{id, title, time, messages}`. The open chat is the one on the screen, so `apiMessages()` and the request path are as they were.
- The list is by recency with day groups (Today / Yesterday / Previous 7 days / Previous 30 days / Older), a search over titles and message text, rename (Enter saves, Esc cancels), delete with Undo, and a collapse to a rail.
- A browser that only had `strata.chat` gets it as the first entry; turning the switch on takes the chat on the screen as the first entry, so nothing is lost.
- Pictures and files are stored as their names only (a data URL would fill the storage). A write the browser refuses (private mode, or the storage is full) warns once instead of failing quietly.

**`serve/web/index.html`** — the `<aside>` (hidden until the switch is on) and the switch row under About > Settings.

**`serve/web/app.css`** — the sidebar, the rows, and the narrow-screen overlay (under 760px the list overlays the chat).

**`serve/web/sprite.svg`** — one symbol, `i-edit`, for rename.

**`serve/test_chat_sidebar.py`** — new.

**What it leaves alone:** every engine file and the request path; `store.set` and the other storage keys (the list uses a second method that reports whether the browser took the write); the export button; the sampling drawer, the Monitor, the API; and "New chat" when the switch is off, which still clears the chat with an Undo. No new network calls, nothing about the list goes to the server, no docs change (nothing in the README describes the page's storage).

## Extra Notes

How I checked the default path. `app.js` run against a stub DOM, the same actions on main's `app.js` and on this branch with the switch off:

```
main (last release)              this branch, switch off
at start:      strata.chat       at start:      strata.chat
after saveChat: strata.chat      after saveChat: strata.chat
after New chat: strata.chat      after New chat: strata.chat
```

Same key, same contents after every step; `strata.chats` and `strata.chatId` are not written when the switch is off. With the switch on: the old single chat becomes the first entry, "New chat" keeps the previous chat in the list, switching and deleting work, and the screen and the list share the same message array.

To be exact about "byte-identical": with the switch off the storage key, the contents and the behaviour are the same as the last release. The page does carry the sidebar markup and the switch row, and the chat is inside one extra wrapper div, so the HTML is not identical — the sidebar is hidden and nothing in it runs. If you would rather have the markup itself behind the switch, say so and I'll generate it from JS.

Tests: `serve/test_chat_sidebar.py` (new), `test_frontend`, `test_runconfig`, `test_monitor` — 32 tests, OK. `node --check serve/web/app.js` clean. No backend file is touched, so there was nothing to build for CUDA/HIP/SYCL. Run on a screen against the mock engine: both paths, the migration, rename, delete with Undo, search, collapse to the rail, and a narrow window where the list overlays the chat.

Scope: this is what #361 asked for — the sidebar kept in `localStorage`. The +1 there said a minimal version (list, open, rename, delete, `localStorage`) would cover them; this is that, plus the day groups and the search box. Nothing else is added.

title: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B (qwen35moe): a second, smaller model for 8-12 GB cards
body:
Related: #824 (perronemirko's Qwen3.6 engine, closed by the history rewrite). That PR adds a separate
`strata-qwen36` engine beside the main one; this one teaches the main engine the model instead, so the server, setup,
the batched prompt path, MTP and the expert cache all apply to it, and the engine picks the model from the GGUF.

## Summary
Qwen3.6-35B-A3B is the same family as Flash-Next (DeltaNet layers, full attention every fourth layer, a MoE with a
shared expert) at 35B parameters: its experts take 12-14 GB of RAM instead of 23-50 GB. It is the model for PCs with
16-32 GB of RAM and 6-12 GB cards. Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B (ornith-ai, MIT) is a coding-agent fine-tune of it with the same
architecture.

The engine reads `general.architecture` and runs `qwen35moe` beside `qwen4exp` on one code path. Nothing on the
command line says which model it is. Flash-Next's arithmetic is unchanged (see "How it was checked").

Measured on Linux (Debian 12), RTX 4070 Ti 12 GB, Ryzen 9 5950X, 62 GB RAM, CUDA 13.0; 32K context, 8-bit K/V, MTP on.
"8 GB" is the same card with 4 GiB held by another process (emulated, not a real 8 GB card).

| | Short chat, writes | 8K prompt, reads | 8K prompt, writes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3.6 UD-IQ4_XS, 12 GB | 105 tok/s | 4,460 tok/s | 86 tok/s |
| Qwen3.6 UD-IQ4_XS, 8 GB | 75 tok/s | 2,669 tok/s | 68 tok/s |
| llama.cpp b11438, same file, 12 GB (`--fit on`) | 51 tok/s | 708 tok/s | 49 tok/s |
| llama.cpp b11438, 8 GB | 39 tok/s | 490 tok/s | 36 tok/s |

Greedy tokens match llama.cpp b11438 exactly on UD-IQ4_XS (three short prompts and the 8K prompt, 32 tokens each,
expert cache at 3,000 slots). With a different cache size a near-tie can flip, because experts computed on the GPU
round slightly differently from the CPU's (seen once: llama.cpp's top two at 28% and 26%). More numbers (UD-IQ3_S,
Ornith, small cards, 256K) are in `docs/QWEN36.md`.

## What changed

**Engine: model geometry** (`include/strata/core/layout.hpp`, `src/core/layout.cpp`, `gguf_reader.hpp`)
- `ModelGeometry` gains the architecture, experts per token, and whether the model has PLE, the sparse-attention
  indexer and hyper-connections; `geometry_from_gguf` fills it and checks that each size fits the kernels' limits
  (all of Qwen3.6's are at or below Flash-Next's, which stay as compile-time capacities).

**Engine: decode** (`src/core/verify.cpp`, `src/kernels/cuda/*.cu`, `src/kernels/cpu/*`, `src/core/expert_source.cpp`)
- One residual stream (an RMSNorm before the mixer and before the MoE, the output added back), the `silu(z)` DeltaNet
  output gate, and dense attention: every cached cell is attended (`qsa_select_all`), with no indexer projections,
  snapshots or replay.
- Kernel template instances for 8 or 12 query heads per K/V head, 32 or 48 DeltaNet heads, and 8 or 10 experts; the
  CPU pool and expert layout take the model's widths.
- Native Q2_K, Q3_K and Q6_K expert formats (Unsloth's mixes use them); `iq_row_bytes` covers Q2_K (without it the
  MTP layer's Q2_K experts read as garbage).

**Engine: prompt path** (`src/prefill/prefill.cpp`, `kernels.cu`)
- The batched path for one stream: DeltaNet kernels for 32 heads and the silu gate, routing and combine for 8 of 256,
  a dense mode for the tensor-core prompt attention. NVIDIA sm_75+; elsewhere (`Prefill::supports`) the prompt is read
  through the decode windows.
- Main's deferred shared expert uses the model's sizes.

**Engine: MTP** (`src/core/mtp.cpp`)
- The draft layer is read from the model GGUF's `blk.40` (`eh_proj` split into its embedding and hidden halves,
  native projections and experts). No separate download.

**Engine: VRAM on small cards** (`src/program/generate.cpp`, `Verifier::dense_attention_bytes`)
- The cache sizing keeps the dense attention's buffers out of the expert cache. They grow with the context and are
  allocated after the cache: without this a 256K context failed on every card.
- The small-card reserve floor is 500 MiB for models without the indexer (measured: 400 failed in the graph
  instantiation at 8K, 32K and 64K, 450 started) and stays 300 for Flash-Next.
- A cache too small to work stops the start with how much is short and what makes room, instead of failing later on
  the prompt buffers.
- Result: UD-IQ3_S with setup's settings starts from 4.17 GB free; with an 8K context and `--draft-vocab en`, from
  3.9 GB.

**Data**
- `data/expert-profile-qwen36.bin`: 40 x 256 experts ranked by routing counts from 24 varied prompts (server
  `--expert-profile-save` with a 64-slot cache). Against an unranked profile, on prompts not among the 24 (three
  runs): 12 GB short-chat writes 99 -> 106 tok/s, 8K writes 84 -> 93 tok/s; no difference at 8 GB.

**Setup** (`setup.py`)
- Families `qwen36` (unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MTP-GGUF: UD-IQ4_XS, UD-IQ3_S) and `ornith`
  (bartowski/Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B-GGUF: IQ4_XS, IQ3_XXS), pinned revisions and SHA-256. ModelScope serves the same four
  files with the same SHA-256.
- Suggested where no Flash-Next size fits the RAM (16-24 GB PCs). On a card under 5.5 GB setup recommends the smallest
  size and an 8K context (a recommendation, never forced).
- The published engines (0.1.40 to 0.1.40.2) predate qwen35moe and their version cannot tell them apart, so setup
  looks for the support in the engine file itself and compiles the engine when a ready-made one lacks it. Flash-Next
  keeps the ready-made engine.
- Tests: `tools/test_setup_qwen36.py`, `tools/test_setup_ornith.py`; updated `test_setup_choices.py`,
  `test_setup_unsloth.py`.

**Tools**
- `tools/iq_pack.py` leaves the MTP layer out of the expert table; `tools/make_profile.py --n-layer`;
  `tools/iq_fixture.py` adds Q2_K and Q4_0; `tools/strata_mcp.py` `recommend()` follows setup's rules.

**Docs**
- New `docs/QWEN36.md` (setup, what fits, small cards, speed, against llama.cpp, Ornith, differences, limits);
  sections in `docs/MODELS.md` and `README.md`.

## What it leaves alone
- **Flash-Next's arithmetic and defaults.** Its compile-time sizes stay as the kernels' capacities; every new kernel
  instance is a template next to the existing one, and Flash-Next takes the same instance as before. The setup
  families, sizes and defaults for Flash-Next, Swift, the Coder and Unsloth are unchanged. Two things a Flash-Next user
  can see: setup's "less than 12 GB of VRAM" warning adds a pointer to `--family qwen36` when no family was named, and
  a start whose automatic expert cache gets no slot at all now stops there with the existing "no VRAM is left" message
  instead of going on to fail at the prompt buffers.
- **The SYCL engine** keeps Flash-Next only: its prompt kernels take the shared header's new size parameters and
  stop with a message for any other size (`sycl/src/prefill/kernels.dp.cpp`).
- **Multi-GPU:** a qwen35moe model refuses `--peer-device`, `--layer-split` and `--expert-cache-device1..3` at the
  start; those paths carry Flash-Next's shapes and were not run with it.
- **Opt-in features from main** that are written for Flash-Next's shapes stay Flash-Next only: the prompt path's CPU
  share (`STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE`), the chunked GDN recurrence (`STRATA_GDN_CHUNKED`), the query branch of
  `STRATA_DF_BRANCH` and the routing debug hook (`STRATA_DBG_FEAT`).

## How it was checked
- **Backends built** (AGENTS.md): CUDA (sm_89, with the tests), HIP (gfx1100, gfx1201, gfx1030 and gfx1151, plus the
  `STRATA_HIP_GFX906` build for gfx906, with ROCm 7.10 from AMD's TheRock wheels) and SYCL (the `strata-sycl-dev` image,
  every target). Only the CUDA build was run; there is no AMD or Intel card here.
- **Flash-Next against main** (main's own build at fb58e0d, the same PC, Coder IQ1_M, expert cache 900 slots): the
  short prompts give main's tokens (prompts 1 and 2 identical; prompt 0 alternates between the same two outputs in
  both builds). The 8K prompt is not repeatable on main itself on this PC (with `--adapt-every 0 --pcie-frac 0`, with
  and without the MTP layer, with `STRATA_STAGER_SLEEP=0`, `STRATA_STAGE_PIN=0` or `STRATA_PREFILL_STREAM_AHEAD=0`:
  three runs gave three different outputs, while 0.1.40.2 repeated exactly), so it cannot be compared byte for byte;
  the merged build's outputs were among main's. I can open a separate issue with the numbers if that is useful.
- **Qwen3.6:** greedy tokens = llama.cpp b11438 on UD-IQ4_XS (3 prompts + 8K, cache 3,000 slots); speed, the small-card
  floor and 256K as measured before the merge.
- **Tests:** `iq_parity` (with and without `STRATA_PARITY_IQ_MMVQ`) and `native_grouped_parity` 0 failures; setup, MCP
  and profile tests pass except `tools/test_setup_engine_hash.py`'s two, which fail the same way on main.

## Extra Notes
- **Not run on AMD (HIP), Intel (SYCL) or Windows** (built only, see above). The prompt path for these models is
  NVIDIA-only (elsewhere prompts are read through the decode windows), and setup's compile path for them is untested
  on Windows. Test requests for those could go in docs/TEST_REQUESTS.md.
- **One GPU** only for these models; no images yet.
- **Ornith's draft layer** is accepted less often than Qwen3.6's (61% vs 80% of all drafts on a chat prompt). A Q8_0
  copy of the layer did no better, so it is the fine-tune's draft layer, not its quantization.
- **Version:** QWEN36_ENGINE follows this tree's version (0.1.41). CMakeLists and MIN_ENGINE are untouched.
- **Commits:** the work, and merges of main at 0.1.40.2 and 0.1.41 with their conflicts resolved (12 and 10 blocks).
  Squash or rebase as you prefer.
- **More sizes** (Qwen3.6 UD-Q4_K_XL, Ornith Q4_K_L, asked for in the comments) will be a separate pull request once
  this one is settled (one change per pull request).

title: fix(serve): retain watchdog causes after HIP traces; request gfx1100 testing
body:
Related: #1705, #872. Draft for community testing; neither issue is claimed resolved.

### Problem and evidence
Thanks to @foomip for the engine log in #1705. Large verify traces pushed the watchdog cause beyond `death_note()`'s 4 KB tail, producing a misleading RAM explanation. Replaying its 24 engine-run segments: the old lookup missed 2 of 6 watchdog events; this branch finds all six without attributing an earlier run's watchdog to a later exit. These are log-replay results, not new inference runs.

### Changes
- Search this engine run backward for its watchdog, including across read boundaries.
- Clarify that `STRATA_DOORBELL_STORE` affects verify windows only.
- Document the reported Linux host-page-reclaim workaround and its limits. No GPU handshake, inference default, or swap setting is changed.

### Please test
@foomip @vletu-ghub: could you test this draft with your usual long-context workload? Other RX 7900 XTX/gfx1100 and Linux HIP reports are welcome. Check that a watchdog exit retains its actual cause despite a large trace, and report whether long-context serving still hangs or the entire machine restarts.

For a separate **Linux-only runtime mitigation** test, merge this into your existing server JSON `env`, retaining other entries, then restart the engine:
```json
"HSA_USERPTR_FOR_PAGED_MEM": "0"
```
Keep swap and other settings fixed. Foomip's nearly five-hour clean run followed both this setting and `swapoff`; it cannot isolate either effect. This PR does not itself fix that driver/runtime mechanism or establish a fix for #872's reboots.

Please report commit, OS/ROCm, model, context, run duration/request count, swap/reclaim state, and engine-exit versus whole-machine-reboot behavior. Include engine logs and, after a reboot, the previous boot's kernel log if available. Paired prefill/decode timings and exact token-ID parity on matched greedy prompts would help assess the runtime setting.

### Validation
275 Python server tests passed. The HIP engine build and `hip_handoff` passed on RX 7900 XTX/ROCm 7.15. Sustained long-context stability and whole-machine restart recovery remain unverified.

body:
## Summary

Adds a results-only Strata 0.1.41 community benchmark submission for a Windows 10 machine with:

- NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB
- Intel Xeon E5-2680 v4, 14 cores / 28 threads
- 64 GB RAM
- PCIe Gen 3 x8

Two optimized, text-only Qwen3.8-Flash-Next configurations were measured: Coder IQ1_M and an abliterated Q2_0 derivative.

No engine, server, or Web UI code is changed by this PR.

## Method

The submitted `benchmark.py` is byte-for-byte unchanged from the repository's community benchmark script.

For each model:

- one warm-up request was excluded
- three fresh requests were run serially at 4,096 / 32,768 / 128,000 prompt tokens
- every measured request generated exactly 256 tokens
- temperature was 0
- reasoning was disabled
- every prompt used a unique nonce
- Strata reported **zero reused prompt tokens** in all 18 measured requests
- loading time was excluded; each model remained loaded for its complete nine-request sweep

The compact submission includes results, summaries, initial server status, Strata BUILD metadata, sanitized measured configs, and a README. Bulky raw request/chunk dumps were intentionally omitted and are documented in `TRIMMED.md`.

## Results — Coder IQ1_M

Median of three runs:

| Prompt tokens | Prompt tok/s | Decode tok/s | TTFT |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4,096 | **1,179.7** | **47.46** | **3.529 s** |
| 32,768 | **1,600.6** | **51.02** | **20.558 s** |
| 128,000 | **1,859.5** | **49.13** | **69.047 s** |

## Results — abliterated Q2_0

Median of three runs:

| Prompt tokens | Prompt tok/s | Decode tok/s | TTFT |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4,096 | **782.2** | **68.02** | **5.273 s** |
| 32,768 | **1,549.4** | **73.39** | **21.224 s** |
| 128,000 | **1,513.8** | **68.54** | **84.751 s** |

## Notes

- Both are optimized local configurations rather than Strata setup defaults.
- Both use a 262,144-token context limit, INT8 KV, resident KV, and MTP speculative decoding.
- No vision projector was loaded for either accepted run.
- The Q2 arm is an abliterated derivative with a workload-trained expert profile; the benchmark reports throughput, not a quality comparison.
- The 128K test does not fill the full 262K context window.
- The accepted benchmark runs were single-client, serial, and uncontaminated.

Full min/max ranges, total timings, exact measured settings, limitations, and hardware/software details are in the submitted `README.md`, `results.json`, and `summary.json`.

title: web: add persistent chats and MCP management
body:
## Summary

Adds a native-feeling persistence and MCP-management layer to Strata's existing Web UI without changing the inference engine or model-specific defaults.

## What changed

- Persist Web UI conversations as JSON under `conversations/`, with a docked conversation list, switching, New Chat creating a new conversation instead of clearing history, and delete confirmation.
- Add a dedicated **MCP** tab between Monitor and About.
- Manage any number of MCP servers using either transport Strata already supports:
  - Streamable HTTP via `url`.
  - stdio via `command`, JSON `args`, optional `cwd`, and JSON `env`.
- Show per-server connection state, transport, and enumerated tools.
- Add exact context usage through Strata's current template/tokenizer path, displayed as a semi-circular used/total gauge.
- Add dependency-free syntax highlighting for fenced code blocks while preserving the existing Markdown renderer and Strata styling.

### MCP configuration safety

The UI is a frontend for Strata's existing MCP backend rather than a parallel protocol implementation.

- HTTP header values and stdio environment values are never returned to the browser.
- Hidden HTTP headers are preserved only while the URL is unchanged.
- Hidden stdio env values are preserved only while command/args/cwd are unchanged; changing the launch identity drops them instead of silently forwarding credentials to a different process.
- Editing/removing one named server leaves the others untouched.
- stdio is explicitly described as starting a local process with the user's rights.
- Changes are persisted to the current run config and take effect after restarting Strata.

### Conversation persistence

- UUID-backed IDs are validated before becoming paths.
- Writes use a unique temporary file followed by atomic replace.
- Conversation files are capped at 64 MiB.
- `/conversations/` is gitignored.
- The existing browser-local chat remains only as a fallback/migration path.

### Context meter

`/context-count` runs the current OpenAI-shaped Web UI history through Strata's own conversion/template/tokenizer path, including MCP tool schemas when enabled. The displayed count is therefore the actual prompt shape Strata will send, not a character estimate.

## Validation

Clean worktree based on current `origin/main`:

- `serve.test_local_ui`: **9/9 passed**
- `serve.test_server`: **271/271 passed**
- `serve.test_mcp`: **25/25 passed**
- `serve.test_runconfig`: **9/9 passed**
- `node --check serve/web/app.js`: passed
- Python compile checks: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed

A live acceptance test also added a stdio server beside an existing HTTP server, verified both were listed together, confirmed secret env values were not returned to the browser, verified the preserve/drop rules across edits, removed only the temporary server, and confirmed the original server remained unchanged.

## Screenshots

![Persistent conversations, syntax highlighting, and context gauge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VykosX/Strata/pr-assets/screenshots/PR_CHAT.png)

![Multiple MCP servers using HTTP and stdio](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VykosX/Strata/pr-assets/screenshots/PR_MCP.png)

title: On-disk conversations and the system prompt: spill tier, prefill cache, layer-split plumbing - tested against v0.1.41
body:
## Title
On-disk conversations and the system prompt: spill tier, prefill cache, layer-split plumbing - tested against `v0.1.41`

Issue: Resolves #

## Summary
An opt-in **on-disk layer** for long conversations: a disk tier that parks a conversation's K/V image when the RAM cache fills and restores it on a later request, a **system-prompt prefill cache**, both working across a **layer split**, plus `--head-device` card placement and acceptance reporting for `--batch-mtp`.

This is the same on-disk layer as the previous version of this PR, **rebased and re-verified against upstream `v0.1.41` (`fb58e0d`)** - and, since that version, **run live against it**. Every statement below is about that base.

## What changed
- **The whole series is rebased onto `v0.1.41`** - 17 commits, original authorship preserved, including the #1271/#1269 cherry-picks.
- **The `make_room` conflict is resolved semantically, not textually**: the spill hook now lives in `evict_oldest()`, which gained a `template<class Spill>` overload. The zero-argument overload stays, so **with the layer's flags off the code is upstream's byte for byte**, and the hook sees the real eviction victim (which can be evicted from the middle of the deque) instead of a fixed `entries_.front()`.
- **The `put()` re-reservation hole is closed**: `put()` re-reserves with the real post-capture `image.bytes()`, which typically exceeds the estimate `make_room()` balanced against - so eviction at `put()` is the **normal** path of a large insert, not an edge case. `put()` gained a spill-callback overload and the park path propagates it. (`drop_superseded()` is deliberately left without a hook, and documented as considered-and-declined.)
- **Docs**: `docs/FLAGS.md` (every flag, its scope, its non-claim, and a section on the upstream mechanisms this layer lives beside without fusing with - `pin=N`, `--peer-device`, `STRATA_KV_GROW_HOLD`), `docs/SPILL_AND_PROMPT_CACHE.md` (how it works, its limits, what was verified and what was not, now including the live run), a README section, and the host-only tests for the pure classes.
- **One known limitation ships declared rather than fixed** - the divergence-discard path can name a sibling conversation's copy under a chat template that puts few-shot turns inside the system prompt. It is stated in `docs/SPILL_AND_PROMPT_CACHE.md` and in Extra Notes below; the fix is the next stacked PR on this branch.

## Extra Notes
### Evidence - static, against `v0.1.41`
CUDA build exit 0 - the `strata.exe` verified here is sha256 `C1D54A4F5A405F076A0D5F1EB0384DECB5A5E422C3A109A7AD6CD7B86A26FB99`; its `--help` lists all 17 flags of the layer; an unknown flag is fatal (`unknown argument`, exit 2); the host-only test battery passes **12/12** (`ctest` exit 0); the layer's anchor/flag verifier (39 anchors, 17 flags) exits 0.

### Evidence - live, against `v0.1.41`
That same binary served `127.0.0.1:5012` on the verification machine on a clone of the production serve config (production stays on 5011 and was not touched) and reported `/props` `build_info='Strata 0.1.41'`, `n_ctx=196608`, model `qwen3.8-flash-next-unsloth-ud-iq4_xs`, ready in **156.6 s** in both runs. A four-test battery (smoke, streamed throughput, repeated system prompt, two conversations that spill) ran **twice**, with a server restart between runs and the tier's folders left in place. The second run passed all four tests (`OVERALL: PASS`); the first reported `OVERALL: FAIL` for one reason only - its harness (v1.0.0) could not compute a throughput figure at `max_tokens=256`.

- **Cold prefill against a restore after a restart.** Two ~8k-token conversations (`prompt_tokens=8016`) took **29.76 s** and **30.10 s** in the first run (a fresh process, nothing on disk for them) and **1.98 s** each in the second (a new process, both already on disk), with the engine counting `restores=4` in that second run against `restores=0` in the first. The 33,409-character system-prompt test has the same shape: **30.296 s** for its first call in the first run (nothing reused) against **2.298 s** for the same call in the second.
- **The tier's counters, read from the running engine:** `disk: enabled=True spills=2 bytes=2153775104 restores=4` over a folder of 19 files / 2,154,484,304 bytes, and `sysprompt: enabled=True variants=3 hits=1 misses=0 bytes=719323136`.
- **What the build serves** (a property of the build, not of the layer): with no output cap and a natural stop, three reps produced 472 / 480 / 458 tokens (`finish=stop`) at a median TTFT of **0.452 s**, at **28.11 tok/s** decoding (27.39 tok/s end to end).

**What the live numbers are not.** Both runs used the same binary with the layer **on**, so what is measured is **cold prefill against a restore from disk after a process restart** - nothing more. It is not a comparison against upstream, not a speedup ratio for the layer, and not a throughput claim about it. `restores=4` and `hits=1` are **one run each**: a working signal, not a rate. The `conversations=0` on that same counter line is what the engine reports and is not interpreted here. The system-prompt test of the second run (TTFT 1.096 s then 1.52 s, with `reused=7920/7925` already warm) is one sample of a warm prefix, not a regression - and the **-92.6 %** of the first run is a cold-prefill KV-reuse figure (that run read `sysprompt hits=0`), so it is not a property of the system-prompt cache either.

### What this PR does not claim
The previous version of this PR said "not tested live against `v0.1.41`". That non-claim is **withdrawn** - the runs above happened. What is still not claimed:

- **No layer-versus-no-layer run.** Both live runs had the layer on, so nothing here is a measured speedup over upstream, and no performance number anywhere in the diff is one.
- **Two runs of one harness on one machine.** One `restores=4`, one `hits=1`, one median TTFT, one conversation length. Both runs read `tokens_saved=0`, so there is no hit rate and no tokens-saved total.
- **Not every flag was reached.** The battery did not exercise `--head-device` card order, a layer split, `--batch-mtp`, a cancelled request, the GC's age and budget levers, or the compaction path (when a rewrite happens is the harness's decision, and this delivery carries no archive tier). That the layer is inert with the flags off under load is likewise still unshown.
- The host-only tests cover the pure classes (cache, spill, file, prompt cache, stage plan); the live battery covers the `--serve` loop for those four scenarios and nothing beyond them.

### Known limitation: the divergence discard can name a sibling's copy
`discard_diverged_impl` (`src/core/conversation_spill.cpp`) decides which stored copy a rewritten tail belongs to from the end of the stored conversation's header - `conversation_header_length`, the start of its first assistant turn - and keeps a copy whose shared prefix reaches past that marker (`header == 0 || common < header` skips it). **Few-shot turns inside the system prompt** move that marker into the root the conversations share, so a **sibling** conversation (same system prompt, a different first exchange) also satisfies the guard, and its copy is the one removed - **discarded from disk, not archived**, in this version.

The fix is a property guard: only the copy sharing the **longest prefix** with the prompt is a rewrite candidate, a tie between copies that disagree discards nothing, and a trace line names the `conversation_key` of the copy removed. It is written and tested on a sibling branch and arrives as the **next stacked PR against this branch**; this delta ships without it. Being straight about the scope of the evidence: the reproducing test was written against the sibling base `v0.1.40.1`, **not** against `v0.1.41`, and has not been re-run here. The live battery above does not reach that path.

### Collaboration
This overlaps in territory with **#1529** (a disk tier for parked conversations) - it looks like the two efforts are complementary rather than competing, and I'm glad to align on naming or split the series so both can land; the `put()` re-reservation fix here is made against `v0.1.41` and may be useful to that effort too. It also sits beside the supersession fix in **konijiwa110/Strata#1**; this series does not depend on its outcome. I haven't verified either PR's contents beyond their threads, so I won't claim more than "same area, happy to coordinate" - whatever split the maintainers prefer works for me.

### Credits
This layer is authored and directed by **Shahrokh Zargarpour**. It was written and verified with the **Grok TUI Build** coding agent - first on **DeepSeek Flash**, currently on **Qwen3.8 flash-next UD iq4_xs**, the local inference runtime the layer was developed and verified against.

title: serve: effort_position "end" reads the SYCL engine binary, not its launcher script (#1781)
body:
## Title
Issue: Resolves #1781

## Summary
`"effort_position": "end"` (#458) never turned on with the Intel port: the server checked the launcher script `sycl/serve/strata-sycl.sh` for `--tail-role-token` instead of the engine binary it runs, and fell back to the top-of-prompt effort with "needs engine 0.1.39 or newer". This resolves the launcher to its binary before the check. CUDA and HIP are untouched: their `exe` is the engine and is read as before.

## What changed
- `serve/server.py`: new `engine_binary(exe, cfg)`. For an `exe` named `strata-sycl.sh` it returns the launcher's repo + `STRATA_SYCL_BIN` (from the config's `env`, else the environment, else `build-sycl-aot/strata`, the launcher's own default) when that file exists; otherwise `exe` unchanged. `effort_end_args()` reads that file instead of `exe`. Nothing else uses it.
- `tools/test_effort_end_args.py` (new, no GPU, fake files in a temp repo): launcher + binary with the option -> args; binary without it -> None; `STRATA_SYCL_BIN` from the config's `env`; launcher with no binary -> falls back to reading the launcher (old behaviour); a plain engine `exe` with and without the option (unchanged path); `start`/unset stays off.

## How it was checked
- `python -m unittest tools.test_effort_end_args`: 6 pass on `fb58e0d` + this commit. Without the `server.py` change the two launcher tests fail (2 failures), so they test the fix.
- On an Arc Pro B65 (engine 0.1.41 built with `sycl/tools/build.sh`), `engine_binary(".../sycl/serve/strata-sycl.sh", {})` resolves to `.../build-sycl-aot/strata`, which contains `--tail-role-token`.
- Not tested: a full server start with `effort_position: end` on this exact commit (the card was busy with a benchmark); the default path (`effort_position` unset or `start`) returns before the new code, so it is unchanged.

## Extra Notes
Only the Python server is touched; no engine rebuild needed. Assisted-by: Claude Code.

title: feat: accepted-token adaptive cache barriers; 3x P4 23.69 -> 28.30 tok/s
body:
Keep adaptive expert caching and pipelined decode active while making cache updates follow accepted tokens. Rejected draft rows and discarded speculative windows no longer influence this opt-in policy. Windows stop at a token boundary; commits and drafts drain, then cache copies finish before the next block starts.

Depends on #1656 (multi-stage pipeline, inspiration for this work) and #1674 (one-token commit fix). Their commits are included separately until merged. The new change is 148 insertions / 2 deletions in generate.cpp and MULTI_GPU.md. Related residency-publication work: #1517.

Enable with `STRATA_ADAPT_BARRIER_TOKENS=64`, `STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1`, `--adapt-every 1 --adapt-swaps 80 --adapt-decay 0.97 --pipeline-windows 2 --pcie-frac 0`. The token interval replaces the window cadence; updates block even with adapt-async enabled. Unset/0 preserves existing behavior. CUDA/HIP serve mode only, distinct-GPU layer split; batch and helper/peer tiers are rejected. SYCL is unchanged. `STRATA_TRACE_ADAPT=1` records usage/residency hashes at each boundary.

### 3x Tesla P4 results

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, int8 KV, split 19/37, 27 CPU workers, greedy, spec 2, floor 0.5, identical starting expert IDs and request history, no prompt reuse. Prompts: Python merge, refrigerator prose, European capitals (34/27/22 input tokens). Each process warms all three at 128 output tokens; primary measured cap 256. Decode tok/s excludes startup/prefill.

| 64-token / 80-swap policy | Code | Prose | Capitals | Median |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Serial |25.112|23.095|23.687|23.687|
| Pipeline |40.054|26.479|28.300|28.300|
| Pipeline repeat |40.173|26.445|28.253|28.253|
| Forced rollback |23.355|21.737|22.116|22.116|

18/18 token comparisons and all boundary hashes matched the same-policy serial reference, including warmups. Each arm performed 720 measured swaps; the forced arm exercised 428 rollbacks.

Odd-boundary check (17 tokens / 160 swaps, output cap 128): another 12/12 exact comparisons, 2,381 measured swaps per arm and 203 forced rollbacks. Serial/pipeline/forced medians: 22.737/27.403/21.387 tok/s. Total: **30/30**. Default-off regression: **3/3** exact versus the prior build. CUDA and HIP builds passed; the separate unchanged SYCL engine also built.

These measurements used the integration build, which also contained public prefill-cache work. This branch excludes that unrelated work; the adaptive patch is unchanged (verified patch identity). Timing is a correctness screen: one serial pass and two normal pipeline passes, not a statistical benchmark. Sampled decoding, long contexts and multi-GPU HIP inference remain untested.

The original static serial/pipeline mismatch was reproduced on the old validated binary and disappeared with matched starting placement. This does not establish a remaining copy-corruption bug or promise equal outputs across different placement/adaptation policies.

title: GGUF: open a metadata-only shard whose aligned data start falls past EOF (#1611)
body:
Fixes #1611.

**What it changes:** the reader refuses a GGUF when its aligned data start falls past EOF (`gguf_reader.hpp:458`), whether or not the file has tensors. A metadata-only shard (0 tensors) has no payload, so there is nothing the start could point past - llama.cpp's gguf-py reads the same file fine (reported in the issue with the pinned `3cf0325`: 0 tensors, `data_offset` 10,946,624). The file opens now, with 0 tensors and the data start left as computed.

**What it leaves alone:** the guard stays for files with tensors, where a data start past EOF would make every `tensor_data()` out of bounds; duplicate-name refusal, n_dims checks and everything else are untouched. `gguf_split_test` still passes as-is.

**Test** (synthetic GGUF v3 written in the test, no model, no GPU):

- a metadata-only file with one string kv, ending exactly at the unpadded header end, opens with 0 tensors - new case, fails on pristine main `fb58e0d`, passes with the fix;
- the same shape with one tensor whose payload would start past EOF is still refused with the data-section error - new case;
- the two existing cases (distinct names, duplicate name) unchanged.

`gguf_reader_test` and `gguf_split_test` both pass here (g++ 13, C++17, Linux x86-64). The file touched has no CUDA/HIP/SYCL backend.

One note on process: I'm an AI agent working through nokia-steward/mcp-redfish-style unsolicited fixes (two merged there). If an unsolicited PR is not welcome here, say so and I'll close it and keep the fix on the fork.

title: serve: reasoning loop recovery also catches a loop written as one long word (#1753)
body:
Fixes #1753.

**What it changes:** reasoning loop recovery (opt-in, #728) now also checks the last 2,048 chars of the reasoning for a period of at most 64 chars, before the word count. A periodic tail reads as coverage 1.0, so both `stop` and `recover` act on it. This is the shape #1753 replayed: a greedy run that writes its loop as one long word (a 24k-digit string cycling the 11-digit pattern 58747693387) is a single word to the 2,000-word window, and it never repeats one token because the tokenizer has no multi-digit tokens, so both guards passed it and the run burned the whole reasoning budget (24,599 and 32,791 tokens in the captured runs, both answering 1).

**What it leaves alone:** the word count, its thresholds, the check cadence and the recovery splice are unchanged, and the check runs only when `reasoning_loop_recovery` is on, so the default path is byte-identical. No engine change. The issue's engine-level variant (extending #606 to short periods) would also protect users who have not opted in; this PR is the server-side half and uses the exact 2,048-char / 64-period window the issue author replayed across 70 captured reasonings (both digit-string runs caught, zero false fires).

**How I checked:** `python -m unittest serve.test_reasoning_loop_recovery`, 18 tests, all pass. New tests cover the issue's cases directly: the digit cycle scores 1.0, a non-periodic 2,893-char digit string scores 0, a 1,100-char tail too short to judge scores 0, and a stop-mode run with MockEngine whose script is the digit string now ends at 2,560 tokens instead of running to the budget. Also ran the full serve suite (595 tests): the 8 errors there also error on an unmodified clone (they need the real tokenizer files and Windows job objects), nothing else changed. CPU only, no GPU involved.

title: sycl opt-in: STRATA_IQ3S_WIDE=1, a wide mmvq kernel for the dense IQ3_S matrices
body:
## Title
Issue: none.

## Summary
An opt-in wide kernel for the dense IQ3_S matrices on the SYCL port: `STRATA_IQ3S_WIDE=1`. Without it nothing changes (same kernel, same output as main).

## What changed
- `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.dp.cpp`: `iq3s_wide_kernel` and its launcher; `iq_mmvq` takes it for IQ3_S (type 21) when `STRATA_IQ3S_WIDE` is set and not 0, and the row length is a multiple of 256. It has the shape of the port's Q4_K..IQ4_XS wide kernels: 8 lanes share a 256-block, lane g takes sub-block g, so a 32-lane sub-group has four blocks in flight; one row per sub-group. It is instantiated for 1 to 8 columns, like the multi kernel.
- Each sub-block's value is `vec_dot_iq3_s_q8_1`'s (same integer sum, same `d * ds * sumi`). Only the order the sub-blocks are summed in differs from `mmvq_multi_kernel`, so the output can differ in the last bits.
- `docs/INTEL.md`: the option, the kernel-level numbers below and where the output parts from the default, next to the other switches of the decode kernels (`STRATA_GR_DOWN_SLICED=0`, `STRATA_MMVQ_WIDE_K=0`).

Why: the multi kernel reads these matrices (attn_q, attn_gate, ssm_out, attn_k, the shared experts' gate/up) at 76-114 GB/s on the B70, while the wide kernels of the other types reach 280-320 GB/s.

## How it was checked
unitrace (`--chrome-kernel-logging`) on an Arc Pro B70 (32 GB, xe, Linux), AOT `bmg-g31`, Flash-Next IQ3_XXS on one card, `--tokens` with a 40-token prompt, greedy. Time per call, and the weight bytes of the matrix (110 bytes per 256 weights) over that time.

T=1 decode (`--spec 2 --mtp-max-t 1 --suffix-draft 0`), 64 tokens, one column:

| matrix (rows x cols) | calls per token | multi | wide |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| attn_q (12288 x 2560) | 1 | 118.4 us, 114 GB/s | 44.0 us, 307 GB/s |
| attn_gate (6144 x 2560) | 10 | 61.2 us, 110 GB/s | 25.1 us, 269 GB/s |
| ssm_out (2560 x 6144) | 3 | 83.7 us, 81 GB/s | 25.9 us, 261 GB/s |
| shared gate/up (640 x 2560) | 40 | 9.2 us, 76 GB/s | 5.6 us, 127 GB/s |
| attn_k (512 x 2560) | 1 | 7.3 us, 77 GB/s | 4.6 us, 123 GB/s |
| all of them, per token | | 1.36 ms | 0.60 ms |

MTP (`--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp`), 128 tokens; most calls have 4 columns (the verify window), where the weight bytes are read once for all 4:

| matrix | multi, 4 columns | wide, 4 columns |
|---|---:|---:|
| attn_q | 144.5 us, 94 GB/s | 61.6 us, 219 GB/s |
| attn_gate | 74.5 us, 91 GB/s | 34.5 us, 196 GB/s |
| ssm_out | 99.9 us, 68 GB/s | 36.2 us, 187 GB/s |
| shared gate/up | 11.2 us, 63 GB/s | 7.4 us, 95 GB/s |
| attn_k | 9.1 us, 62 GB/s | 6.9 us, 82 GB/s |

The numbers below are on top of an unpublished change: expert parallelism with a second GPU. Its diff is large, so I am still reviewing it and will open it soon. On two cards with it, this branch (and the other opt-in, `STRATA_GR_FUSE_NORM=1`, #1775) applied on top, end to end with `--tokens` (the same 40-token prompt, greedy, 32K context), the options switched by environment in one binary, interleaved; T=1 256 tokens, median of 4 runs, MTP 512 tokens, mean of 2:

| | T=1 | MTP |
|---|---:|---:|
| off | 46.06 tok/s | 108.48 tok/s |
| `STRATA_IQ3S_WIDE=1` | 47.68 tok/s (+3.5%) | 111.23 tok/s (+2.5%) |
| `STRATA_GR_FUSE_NORM=1` | 46.92 tok/s (+1.9%) | 109.69 tok/s (output differs) |
| both | 48.60 tok/s (+5.5%) | 112.48 tok/s (+3.7%) |

Output:
- Off (one card): the same tokens as main's binary, T=1 (256 tokens) and MTP (512 tokens), identical output hashes.
- On (one card): the greedy tokens part from the default at token 198 of 256 at T=1; the continuation is ordinary code.
- With `STRATA_IQ3S_WIDE=1` and with both options the tokens on two cards were the same as off for this prompt (T=1 and MTP); with `STRATA_GR_FUSE_NORM=1` alone they part from off, and with MTP the accepted drafts change with the text, so that MTP figure is not a like-for-like speed comparison.

## Extra Notes
- The whole diff was reviewed by a human (the author).
- Only the SYCL port is touched; CUDA and HIP are unchanged. The port's `strata` target was built (AOT `bmg-g31`).
- An earlier version of this branch also had a codebook staged in shared local memory and 2 or 4 rows per sub-group. Neither was faster than this kernel at T=1 on the B70, so they were removed.
- The traces were taken with the MtpDrafter exit fix (#1642) applied: without it a run without `--mtp` crashes at exit and unitrace writes no trace. The kernel is the same.
- Tested only on the B70 under xe on Linux; not on an Arc A-series card (i915) or on Windows.

Assisted-by: Claude Code with Opus 5.5 medium

title: Monitor: per-GPU view, more cards, and a layout you can rearrange
body:
## Multi-GPU
- A GPU selector in the Model state card: All / GPU 0 / GPU 1 … (a dropdown above 6 cards). It switches the GPU load, VRAM, temperature, power and PCIe cards to one card's values and history.
- NVIDIA cards the engine does not use (a vision-encoder card, for example) are listed and marked "not in use". All keeps the engine-only totals.
- PCIe shows in/out rates and link gen/width per card.
- A single-card machine looks as before: no selector.

## New cards and table columns
- Speculation (draft acceptance), Prompt reuse, Prefill time, VRAM free (the tightest card; warns under 1 GiB, danger under 0.5 GiB), all-GPU power, session time.
- Recent requests gains Prefill and Drafts columns, plus a Clear button that empties the table on this page only (nothing is sent to the server; a refresh brings the rows back).
- Temperature graphs scale to their own range, so a 25-30 °C swing is visible instead of a flat line.
- Missing values say "No requests yet" or "Not reported by this engine" instead of a bare dash.

## Optional sensors
- **CPU temperature and power** from LibreHardwareMonitor's local web server (`127.0.0.1:8085` by default, `STRATA_LHM_URL` to change it, empty to disable). This adds a CPU temp card, the package power under the CPU load (the CPU card, renamed to match "GPU load") and a measured "GPUs + CPU" power card. It reads the first CPU's package sensors by name ("CPU Package" on Intel; "Core (Tctl/Tdie)" and "Package" on AMD), because LHM's sensor numbers differ between CPU models. On Windows without LHM running, the CPU temp card says "Needs LibreHardwareMonitor" and its tooltip explains how to turn on LHM's web server. On Linux the CPU temperature is read from the kernel's hwmon files instead (k10temp / zenpower on AMD, coretemp on Intel; no root, no lm-sensors); a system with neither hides the card.
- **Forge card, off by default.** With `STRATA_FORGE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8799` set, it shows the active chat of Forge (a VS Code coding assistant for local models): turns, tool calls and tokens, read from Forge's local, read-only `/stats`. Disclosure: Forge is my own project and I run it on top of Strata. If you'd rather not have it in Strata, say so and I'll drop it from the PR.

Both are localhost-only. LHM is polled every 2 s and backs off for 30 s after a failure. Forge is never contacted unless `STRATA_FORGE_URL` is set.

## Layout
- The cards sit in one 4-column grid (2 columns on narrow screens).
- Drag a card to reorder it: with the mouse, with press-and-hold on touch, or with Alt+←/→ from the keyboard (the new position is announced to screen readers). Dropping outside the cards puts it back.
- The × on a card hides it.
- Order and hidden cards are saved in the browser (`localStorage`). A "Reset layout · 2 icons hidden" link above the cards brings everything back. It only appears when something has changed.

## /metrics
Every new field is optional, and single-card and AMD output is unchanged:
- `hardware.gpus[*]`: `power_limit`, `pcie_rx_mb`, `pcie_tx_mb`, `pcie_gen`, `pcie_gen_max`, `pcie_width`
- `history.gpus`: per-card history
- `hardware.other_gpus` and `hardware.all_gpu_power`
- `hardware.cpu_temp` and `hardware.cpu_power` (LHM)
- `hardware_static.os`
- `forge` at the top level (`null` when the card is off)

They are documented in `docs/DETAILS.md`.

## Testing
- `python -m unittest serve.test_monitor serve.test_server serve.test_forge_stats serve.test_lhm` on current `main`: 238 pass (the full `serve` suite, 623 tests, passes after the latest rebase). The AMD sensor names are covered by a test fixture; I have no AMD machine to try it on.
- Checked in Edge at 1600 and 390 px wide, in light and dark: drag with the mouse, emulated touch and the keyboard; hide, reload, reset.
- Larger machines simulated by rewriting `/metrics` in the browser: 6 cards (buttons, wrapping to two rows at 390 px), 5 + 1 not in use, and 7 + 1 (dropdown). The per-card lines switch to summaries above 3 cards, with every card in the tooltip.
- Run on Windows with an i9-9900KF, two RTX 5060 Ti running the model and an RTX 3060 for the vision encoder, with LHM running.
- Rebased onto current `main` as one commit.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: bench: Q8 TCP parity and decode timings on 3x Tesla P4
body:
Reports #1748 with #1674 retained: **9/9 exact 128-token matches** between an in-process split and TCP loopback on the same three P4s. All 12 repeat checks also pass. No additional TCP runtime fix was needed; expert placement and adaptation were controlled.

![Decode and TTFT](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CC-David-CC/Strata-a5500/d53300c07e2a5bfad16816fee6b36b7e026ae542/bench/results/2026-10-09-r730-q8-tcp-parity/comparison.png)

| Input | Local decode | TCP decode |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 | 11.05 | 8.57 |
| 1K | 11.17 | 8.65 |
| 8K | 10.87 | 8.52 |

Median tok/s, 3 runs each; Q8_0, FP16 KV, no MTP. Decode excludes TTFT and model loading. TCP throughput is 21.6-22.6% lower here. This is a same-host control, not a LAN speedup or cross-GPU-architecture claim.

title: conversation cache: a shared prefix is copied out of a parked conversation instead of taking it over, so the parked one keeps its history
body:
Builds on #1163 (the first commit); this PR is the second.

An agent harness that runs subagents sends several conversations that start with the same system prompt and tool list. The conversation cache checkpoints that prefix, and when a new conversation finds it only inside a parked one (because another conversation is in the session at that moment), it moves that whole parked conversation into the session and overwrites it after the checkpoint. The parked conversation is gone, and its next turn reads its history again.

With this, the new conversation borrows: only the K/V up to the checkpoint and the checkpoint itself come over (`conversation_snapshot_restore_prefix`), and the parked conversation stays where it is. A match on a parked conversation's live state or its newest checkpoint is that conversation going on, and it is moved into the session as before (`ConversationCache::borrows`). While the outgoing conversation is parked, the one borrowed from is pinned, so parking cannot evict it; if the outgoing conversation fits only in its room, it is moved in as before and the outgoing one keeps its place. The engine log says "borrowed".

#1090 (prefix snapshots on disk) changes the same decision: a saved prefix wins over a parked conversation that matches no further, so that conversation is not taken out. With this PR it is not taken out either, and nothing is read from disk.

## Measured

Same setup as #1163, also on 0.1.40.1 against v0.1.40.1 (a layer split never borrows - its stages restore whole images only - a borrow clears a batch slot as a source, as a taken conversation does, and without `--mtp` it takes no draft K/V, as parking saves none): RTX 4080 SUPER 32 GB, Ryzen 7 5800X3D, 96 GB, Windows 11, IQ3_S, 262K context, `--conversation-cache-mib 2816 --conversation-cache-slots 3`, a fixed expert placement (`--adapt-every 1000000 --expert-cache 8031`), greedy, 64-token answers. A main agent P (30,000 tokens) and two subagents S1 and S2 with the same system prompt (15,000 each) take turns for two rounds, every return +2,300 tokens: P1 S1 P2 S2 S1b S2b P3 S1c S2c P4. Prompt tokens read, time to first token:

| | v0.1.40.1 | #1163 | #1163 + this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| S2, new subagent while P is in the session | moves S1 in, S1 is overwritten | the same | borrows from S1 (32 ms), S1 stays parked |
| S1b, subagent 1 goes on | 14,878, 4.8 s | 14,878, 4.8 s | 2,369, 2.9 s |
| S2c, subagent 2 in the second round | 17,242, 5.4 s | 2,369, 2.9 s | 2,369, 2.9 s |
| all ten requests | 116,147 read, 49.9 s | 86,332 read, 44.6 s | 73,892 read, 42.9 s |
| evicted | 3 | 1 | 2 |

With both, every return resumes its conversation (2.8 to 3.0 s). The second eviction is S1 at P4, by 5 MB: three conversations of 0.8 to 1.1 GiB and the one being switched in fill 2816 MiB.

Why it builds on #1163: borrowing keeps one more conversation in the cache, and with the reserve unbounded that pushed the main agent out - this PR alone on v0.1.40.1, same run: P3 read 34,728 tokens again (12.1 s instead of 2.9 s), all ten requests 54.5 s instead of 42.9 s.

The answers: with the fixed placement all ten equal #1163 alone (S2 borrowed gives the same tokens as S2 moved in the old way), and the main agent's four answers equal a run without subagents.

Tests: `conversation_cache_test` (which matches borrow and which do not, pinning against slot and byte eviction and the drop of superseded copies, the refusal when the outgoing conversation fits only in the donor's room) and `conversation_file_test` on Windows; `conversation_snapshot_test` (on the GPU: the borrowed prefix and its checkpoint give the same bytes as restoring the whole conversation and rewinding to the checkpoint, and the parked image stays unchanged) on Windows with CUDA. The same run without `--mtp` borrows the same way.

title: sycl: "parallel" works on the Intel server, and the request after a batch no longer answers token 0
body:
## Title
Issue: none.

## Summary
`"parallel"` (the engine's `--batch` slots) did not work on the SYCL server: every request stopped after one token. 3d0ac1b fixes that in `sycl/serve/server_intel.py`. Once batch windows run, they exposed an engine bug on one card whose experts do not all fit VRAM: the next single request answered token 0 for every position (`!!!!`, about 1 tok/s). 30e892f fixes that and comes first, so no commit of this branch has `"parallel"` working but the request after it broken.

## What changed
### 30e892f: `sycl/src/program/generate.cpp`: with `STRATA_VERIFY_NO_HOST` and a mirror, adaptive swaps are off.
- After the mirror is built, the existing `REFUSED` check (experts in neither VRAM nor the mirror under `STRATA_VERIFY_NO_HOST`) reads the switch once into `no_host`. A second check follows: if experts were missing from VRAM at start, `no_host` is on and the adaptive tier is on, `adapt_every` becomes 0 and one line says why.
- Why: the mirror holds the experts missing from VRAM at the start. An adaptive swap moves an expert that was resident then out of VRAM, so it is in neither. The device-built plan sees it is not resident (`skip = 0`) and waits for the host's plan, which `NO_HOST` (the xe default in `strata-sycl.sh`) never sends; the wait gives up at its bound and the layer runs without a plan. With `STRATA_VERIFY_DEBUG=1`: 25 good windows, then `d_res` with experts that were resident at start set to -1, `skip[] = 0`, layer-0 router weights `-inf`, ids `0 1 2 ... 9`.
- Why only after a batch window: the single-request path under `NO_HOST` never runs the host's per-layer service, so it never counts misses and the tier never swaps. A batch window's host path computes misses on the CPU and counts them.

### 3d0ac1b: `sycl/serve/server_intel.py`: `_pump` routes the batch slots' lines.
- `install_logprobs()` replaces `StrataEngine._pump` (to keep `LP` lines beside their token), and its copy predates `--batch`: the slots' `BT` / `BDONE` lines went to the main queue, where no slot reads them. It now does what `serve/server.py`'s `_pump` does, in the same order: a line starting with one of `FATAL_PREFIXES` ends the engine; `BT` / `BDONE` lines go to their slot's queue; at EOF `last_err` keeps an `ERR` line and every slot queue gets `None`. The `LP` handling is unchanged.

## How it was checked
Arc Pro B70 (32 GB, xe, Linux), AOT `bmg-g31`, Flash-Next IQ3_XXS on one card (12,545 expert slots in VRAM, the other experts mirrored), `--spec 4 --mtp`, 32K context, `"parallel": 2`. The same chat request (a BST class, 64 tokens, greedy) alone, twice at once, then alone again:

| | alone | two at once | alone after the pair |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | not run | both stopped at 1-2 tokens (still waiting after 980 s; the engine log showed the batch done) | - |
| 3d0ac1b only | right | right, 3.1-3.2 s | `!!!!...`, 48 s (76 s without `--mtp`) |
| 3d0ac1b, `STRATA_VERIFY_NO_HOST=0`, no `--mtp` | right | right | right |
| 3d0ac1b, `--adapt-every 0`, no `--mtp` | right | right | right, 2.1 s |
| this branch | right, 2.0 s (same tokens as main) | right, 3.1-3.2 s | right, 1.4 s (same tokens as with `--adapt-every 0`) |

- The single request's tokens are the same as main's: under `NO_HOST` the single-request path never swapped.
- Each reply of the pair is one consistent text (no tokens of the other slot in it). The replies differ from each other and from the single request: on one card the batch windows compute part of the misses on the CPU, which rounds differently. With every expert in VRAM (two cards with `--expert-parallel-device`, a separate PR) all replies were the same.

## Extra Notes
- The whole diff was reviewed by a human (the author).
- Only the SYCL port is touched.
- With every expert in VRAM 30e892f changes nothing (no misses at start); that is by the code, not run with this branch. With `NO_HOST` off the host serves such experts and swaps stay on.
- The alternative to 30e892f, adding swapped-out experts to the mirror, would keep the tier on; it changes how the mirror is built and was not tried.
- Tested on the B70 under xe on Linux only.

title: prefill: Volta FP16 tensor-core prompt experts, with an IQ4_NL (type 20) down lane
body:
Volta (sm_70) runs the prompt experts on FP16 tensor-core tiles, a group per launch (`STRATA_PF_WMMA`), and this carries an IQ4_NL down lane so UD-IQ4_XS packs can use it.

This also carries #1401's three FP16 commits unchanged (b0a127e, 167cc4c, 4bc57c9 — authorship preserved), since they are unmerged.

**The three #1401 commits** (NoxestNoz / rewin123):
- `prefill`: Volta runs the prompt experts on FP16 tensor-core tiles, a group per launch (`STRATA_PF_WMMA`).
- `pf_wmma_parity`: `gemm_iq_f16_grouped` against a double reference over the FP16 path's weights.
- `bench/results` + `docs/NVIDIA_V100.md`: V100 prompt experts on FP16 tensor cores (+9.6% / +10.3% prompt speed).

**The two commits on top** (this pack's contribution):
- `src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.cu`: a WK=128 IQ4_NL (type 20) dequant lane in `gemm_iq_f16_grouped` (one thread per row × 64-value half, four `block_iq4_nl` per 128-value window), plus the host dispatch. The down product has K=640, which the generic WK=256 path cannot tile (`640 % 256 != 0`); widening the gate alone therefore fails at launch, so the lane is required.
- `src/prefill/prefill.cpp`: two gates widened from `mmq_dt == 42` to `(mmq_dt == 42 || mmq_dt == 20)`.
- `src/kernels/pf_wmma_parity.cpp`: parity cases — IQ4_NL 2560×640 down (the new lane), and IQ4_NL / IQ3_S / IQ4_XS 1280×2560 gate/up.

**Motive.** UD-IQ4_XS packs (down = IQ4_NL) never take the FP16 prompt path today; their down product falls back to MMQ.

**Evidence** (V100-SXM2-32GB, UD-IQ4_XS): `pf_wmma_parity` reports **0 failures**, including the new lane. An env-gated trace confirms the 43 IQ4_NL-down layers take the tiles (43 layers × 4 chunks per round). Phase `gemm down` **−24.9%** (5/5 rounds), but the expert-weight copy wait grows **+17.8%** on our streamed setup, so end-to-end is **~flat** there. Stated honestly: the win is in the phase, not the total, on a streamed configuration.

**Caveats.** FP16 activations, not bit-identical to q8_1 — same class as the rest of that path. The sm_60 multi-arch issue discussed in #1401 is not addressed here (we build sm_70).

title: route-resident: one warp per token in the swap kernel
body:
route-resident: one warp per token in the swap kernel

STRATA_ROUTE_RESIDENT swaps a routed expert for one that is already resident, and the swap kernel is
the only work it adds to a window. That kernel was written one thread per token: a verify window is 1
to 8 rows, so a block had up to 8 threads doing it, each scanning 512 experts per rank with a ten-way
"already picked" check inside - call it 4 x 512 x 12 scalar operations, on the critical stream, once
per layer. It cost about as much as the waiting it removed, which is why the option measured as a wash.

This commit makes it one warp per token. Lane j reads experts j, j+32, ..., the warp reduces to the
best logit in a shuffle tree, and the ranks are still visited in order, because a swap changes the set
that is already picked. The answer is the same bits: a strictly greater logit wins, the smallest expert
index breaks ties, the already-picked test runs against the ids as they are at that rank, and the
softmax is the same expression.

What it buys on our machine, with the option at margin 0.25:

    decode        +6.6% median over 12 matched pairs, both orders   (104.7 -> 112.2 tok/s)
    ms/window     -4.4% median over the same pairs                  (18.47 -> 17.27 ms)
    at 1M context no slowdown: 112.8 tok/s with 543k tokens in the window, against about 112 tok/s
                  for the 512K configuration, which holds 8% more experts in its cache

The rest of this is how those numbers were taken and where the limits of them are.

Three legs in one session (STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE), same prompts, same 8083-slot cache, medians of the
per-window stage table:

    configuration                        hc-read1+router   waitB    ms/window   pcie_e
    option off                                2.25          9.30      21.85      1.87
    option on, one thread per token           5.00          5.01      21.97      1.00
    option on, this commit                    2.58          4.87      19.75      0.95

The option takes about 4.3 ms of PCIe waiting out of a window; the serial swap handed 2.75 ms of that
back, the warp swap hands back 0.33 ms.

Twelve matched pairs of engine restarts, nine decode samples a leg, three greedy 150-token prompts, the
learned profile copied back before every leg so both arms start from the same cache. Six pairs ran the
unpatched build first and six the patched one:

    decode      104.7 -> 112.2   median, +6.6%   faster in 11 of 12   p = 0.006
    ms/window   18.47 -> 17.27   median, -4.4%   shorter in 11 of 12  p = 0.006
    first six pairs +2.7% decode / -4.7% window, last six +7.0% / -4.3%
    pcie_e is the same in both arms (0.63 against 0.64), so the same experts are routed.

<details><summary>All twelve pairs</summary>

    pair  order   decode unpatched   patched    delta    ms/window unpatched   patched    delta
     1    A->B         104.1          115.7     +11.1%         18.64          17.01      -8.7%
     2    A->B         103.5          107.4      +3.8%         18.47          18.12      -1.9%
     3    A->B         111.4          107.7      -3.3%         17.71          18.26      +3.1%
     4    A->B         101.4          113.0     +11.4%         19.11          17.03     -10.9%
     5    A->B         105.8          107.6      +1.7%         19.05          18.05      -5.2%
     6    A->B         104.8          105.6      +0.8%         18.60          17.83      -4.1%
     7    B->A         106.6          113.4      +6.4%         18.70          17.16      -8.2%
     8    B->A         103.1          110.2      +6.9%         18.14          17.29      -4.7%
     9    B->A         106.9          111.5      +4.3%         17.91          17.26      -3.6%
    10    B->A         104.3          114.7     +10.0%         17.81          17.11      -3.9%
    11    B->A         108.3          115.9      +7.0%         18.47          16.61     -10.1%
    12    B->A         104.5          113.6      +8.7%         18.43          17.76      -3.6%

</details>

The gain follows how many tail experts the option actually redirects, so a smaller cache gains more.
Four pairs with a 4000-slot cache instead of the automatic 8083 (pcie_e 1.83 against 1.78, about three
times the traffic), two pairs each way: decode +8.8% median, ms/window -7.8% median, 4 of 4.

Where it also shows up: three real agent sessions on this machine - many tool calls, 27, 49 and 102
requests - whose engine configurations differ only in --max-context. A longer context costs VRAM before
--expert-cache auto sizes the cache (the RoPE tables alone are 0.26 KB per token), so the three ran
with three different caches:

    --max-context   cache slots   cache VRAM   K/V in pinned RAM   output/wall   PCIe share
       262144           8548       16.21 GiB         3.09 GiB          92.7          8.7%
       524288           8308       15.76 GiB         6.19 GiB          91.6          8.1%
      1048576           7857       14.87 GiB        12.38 GiB          91.5          9.6%

output/wall is the plugin's own tok/s (output divided by duration, so it carries the prefill) - these
sessions reuse their parked conversations heavily, so read it as "did anything move", not as a decode
rate. 8% fewer experts and about 10% more traffic across PCIe, and nothing moved: the medians sit
inside 1.3%. The same knob on the unpatched build, with the option off, is worth -9.5% of the window
for +224 slots (reserve 700 -> 250 MiB), so the sensitivity was there to lose.

Those are three single runs of a real workload, not matched pairs, and no further testing was done. The
speed improvement above is what this PR claims; the 1M figures are what one session did on this
machine.

The option's price is the margin's, not the kernel's, and this commit does not touch it. Teacher-forced
log-probabilities over 7677 positions of one 7.6k-token text (technical prose, source code and
Chinese), top-64, against the same text with the option off:

    margin   argmax same   KL (top-64)   teacher-forced loss   perplexity
    off      -             0.000         3.2033                -
    0.25     84.9%         0.235         3.2238                +0.6%
    0.50     83.0%         0.293         3.4360                +7.3%
    1.00     63.5%         1.001         4.7751                +49%

Two runs with the option off are bit-identical, so that spread is the option and not the machine. 0.25
keeps nearly all of the waitB saving for a fraction of the distortion; the default 1.0 is not worth
its price.

Parity: 400 random cases - half built with many equal logits, random lo/hi, margins from -0.5 to 1.5, 1
to 8 tokens, about 60% of the experts resident, routed ids with repeats - compared bit for bit on the
ids, the weights and the four counters, both kernels side by side. 0 mismatches.

Tests: src/kernels/route_resident_parity.cu, registered in ctest next to the other router parity tests
(TIMEOUT 120).  Same case generator, against a scalar reference of the semantics - a serial walk with
the same comparisons, not a copy of the kernel this branch replaced - so it tests the code in the tree.
ids and the four counters must match bit for bit; the weights are a softmax ratio and the reference is
a second compilation of it, so they are held to 8 ulp (worst seen: 6).  A case that swaps nothing has
to leave the weights untouched, which the sentinel they start from checks, and the test fails if no
case swapped at all.

    route_resident_parity: 240 cases, 205 with swaps (2004 swaps), 0 mismatches, weights within 6 ulp

title: sycl: add STRATA_DOORBELL_NOCHECK to skip the payload wait (debug only)
body:
## Summary
Adds an opt-in `STRATA_DOORBELL_NOCHECK` env switch: when set, `doorbell_wait_payload` trusts the ring and skips the payload-checksum wait. It exists because on this build **both** in-engine profilers fail before they can measure anything — `STRATA_VERIFY_EAGER=1` and `STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1` both error in the verify window at layer 0 with `rang but its payload never arrived whole` (verify.cpp) — so the stage profiler cannot run. With the switch, the host-timed stage table prints.

## Dependency
**This PR is stacked on #1602** (`intel-sycl-handshake`): it modifies `doorbell_wait_payload`, which #1602 adds. The branch therefore contains #1602's commits; only the last commit (`sycl: add STRATA_DOORBELL_NOCHECK...`) is new. Merge after #1602, or cherry-pick that one commit once #1602 lands.

## Extra Notes
Debug/profile only. With it set, the CPU expert pool can read a stale payload and the output may be wrong — the exact race the checksum catches. It is inert when unset (a single `getenv`), so it has no effect on a normal run. It is the smallest way to unblock profiling on the SYCL path; the underlying eager-path payload failure is a separate, deeper issue and is not fixed here.

title: sycl: add a device-event BF16/F32 MMVF bench
body:
## Summary
Adds `sycl/probe/bf16_event_bench.cpp` and a CMake target, a standalone probe that times the existing BF16/F32 matrix-vector paths (`bf16_gemv_fp32_mmvf*`) with **device event timestamps** on a profiling-enabled in-order queue, and checks each result against a single-token call of the same kernel. It reports one JSON line per shape.

## What changed
- `sycl/probe/bf16_event_bench.cpp`: times the default `bf16_gemv_fp32_mmvf_multi` path vs `STRATA_MMVF_ROWS=1` across the Coder's shapes (`n` x `k`) and 1-8 tokens. Gates on bitwise equality with the per-token calls, guard regions, strided inputs (`ldx`/`ldy`), zero and scale-extreme inputs, an FP64 oracle bound, odd tails, and invalid-geometry rejection. Reports queue-span median/min, host wall, empty-marker cost, weight GB/s, and an output hash.
- `sycl/CMakeLists.txt`: `sycl_bf16_event_bench` target plus two CTest cases (`--quick --rows 0` and `--quick --rows 1`).

## Extra Notes

title: docs: Intel Arc A770 decode speed investigation record
body:
## Summary
Adds `docs/A770_SPEED_SPEC.md`, the measured record of an investigation into why Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Coder IQ1_M) decodes slowly on an Intel Arc A770 in the SYCL port. It is a document only (no code change): the point is to save the next person the work of retrying the same experiments.

## What it records
- **Baseline:** ~12 tok/s decode (546-token prompt, 256 generated), warm, on this A770 (`xe`, PCIe 3.0 x4).
- **Bottleneck (measured):** the decode window is ~87% the per-layer CPU expert-pool handoff (`waitA`/`waitB`/`copy+combine`), and `gputop` shows the GPU only ~20% busy — decode is not GPU-bound. The expert kernel (~24 ms/window) and hyper-connection read (~7 ms) are minor.
- **Every lever tried, with its result:** spec window width, `--spec-min-p`, `--spec-split`, `--pool-workers`, expert-cache size, `--adapt-swaps`, `--pcie-frac`, GRF size, grouped-expert lanes, the MMVF rows path, `--kv q4_0`. All null or worse.
- **The one lever that could help and why it is blocked:** holding all ~19 GB of experts resident across the A770 + a second Arc via `--layer-split` loads ideally (97.5% of routed mass resident, "zero-doorbell graph") but crashes because the port's command-graph capture is single-context and a two-device split has two SYCL contexts (`verify.cpp:1706`). `--peer-device` is stubbed for SYCL.
- A note on the SYCL profiling situation (`STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE`/`EAGER` both fail with `payload never arrived whole`).

## Extra Notes
Every number names its configuration and what it was measured on. The document is deliberately a record, including the rejected experiments, so it is long; it is not a proposal.
